historical_references.reference: The name Ayanv occurs in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, in the context of the Kurukshetra War. Ayanv is mentioned as the name of a sage who lived during the Mahabharata period and had the power to throw a curse on Bhishma Pitamaha (Grandfather of Bhishma), the supreme commander of the Kaurava army. This curse prevented Bhishma from lying down on a bed, as a result of which he chose to lie on a bed of arrows.

Another reference to the name Ayanv can be found in the Hindu scripture, the Puranas. In this context, Ayanv is mentioned as the name of a king who ruled over the region of Kashmir during the Satya Yuga (Golden Age). Ayanv is said to have performed great tapasya (penance) and was blessed with a boon that made him immortal, making him rule over the region for several thousand years.
